title: Streptavidin Immobilization Stress Test
author: Jorge Fernández
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8h3ht8n

steps.title: Prepare nitrocellulose membranes
steps.instruction: Cut the nitrocellulose membranes into rectangles of 0.8 cm x 4 cm dimensions.

substeps.instruction: Cut 2 rectangles from FF170HP nitrocellulose (for a total of 4 pieces).

steps.title: Stamp microfluidic design
steps.instruction: Stamp the microfluidic design following the wax priming protocol on specific membranes.

substeps.instruction: Stamp one piece of FF170HP nitrocellulose membrane.
Stamp one piece of FF80HP nitrocellulose membrane.

steps.title: Attach absorbent pads
steps.instruction: Glue absorbent pads (0.8 cm x 1.2 cm) with tape to the top edge of all 4 nitrocellulose pieces.

steps.title: Deposit streptavidin solution
steps.instruction: Apply streptavidin solution to the 4 pieces of nitrocellulose using a micropipette.

substeps.instruction: Repeat this deposition 3 times, allowing the drop to dry between each application.

steps.title: Dry membranes
steps.instruction: Dry the pieces overnight at 4ºC in a desiccator.

steps.title: Perform thin-layer chromatography
steps.instruction: Conduct thin-layer chromatography using PBS-Tween as the solvent.

substeps.instruction: Pour 15 ml of PBS-Tween solvent into the container.
Position the pieces (individually or all 4 at once) with the absorbent pad touching the bottom of the container.
Allow the solvent to flow through the nitrocellulose for 15 min.

steps.title: Air dry
steps.instruction: Let the pieces dry at room temperature for 40 min.

steps.title: Reveal with Ponceau
steps.instruction: Reveal the membranes by immersing the nitrocellulose pieces into a solution of 0.1% Ponceau within 5% acetic acid for a few seconds.

steps.title: Destain membranes
steps.instruction: Destain the pieces in dH2O with agitation for 2 min.
